lines.text: Bigger number, bigger shield? On a sunscreen, not the way you'd think.
lines.phonemes: bˈɪɡə nˈʌmbə, bˈɪɡə ʃˈiːld? ˌɒn ɐ sˈʌnskɹiːn, nˌɒt ðə wˈeɪ juːd θˈɪŋk.

lines.text: The number isn't a percentage. It's a ratio: how much more burning light your skin can take under the film before it reddens.
lines.phonemes: ðə nˈʌmbəɹ ˌɪzənt ɐ pəsˈɛntɪdʒ. ɪts ɐ ɹˈeɪʃɪˌəʊ: hˌaʊ mˈʌtʃ mˈɔː bˈɜːnɪŋ lˈaɪt jɔː skˈɪn kan tˈeɪk ˌʌndə ðə fˈɪlm bɪfˌɔːɹ ɪt ɹˈɛdənz.

lines.text: Flip it, and fifty lets through about a fiftieth of that light, a hundred about a hundredth, which is barely more blocked.
lines.phonemes: flˈɪp ɪt, and fˈɪfti lˈɛts θɹuː ɐbˌaʊt ɐ fˈɪftiəθ ɒv ðat lˈaɪt, ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd ɐbˌaʊt ɐ hˈʌndɹədθ, wˌɪtʃ ɪz bˈeəli mˈɔː blˈɒkt.

lines.text: But look at what actually gets in: the bigger number lets in half as much, if the film is as thick as the lab's.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt lˈʊk at wɒt ˈaktʃuːəli ɡˈɛts ˈɪn: ðə bˈɪɡə nˈʌmbə lˈɛts ɪn hˈɑːf az mˈʌtʃ, ɪf ðə fˈɪlm ɪz az θˈɪk az ðə lˈabz.

lines.text: Real people, studies found, spread a quarter to half as much as the lab, and protection falls well below the label, by an amount still argued over.
lines.phonemes: ɹˈiəl pˈiːpəl, stˈʌdiz fˈaʊnd, spɹˈɛd ɐ kwˈɔːtə tə hˈɑːf az mˈʌtʃ az ðə lˈab, and pɹətˈɛkʃən fˈɔːlz wˈɛl bɪlˌəʊ ðə lˈeɪbəl, baɪ ɐn ɐmˈaʊnt stˈɪl ˈɑːɡjuːd ˈəʊvə.

lines.text: That lab layer is about as thick as the dead layer under it, a fifth of a sheet of paper.
lines.phonemes: ðat lˈab lˈeɪəɹ ɪz ɐbˌaʊt az θˈɪk az ðə dˈɛd lˈeɪəɹ ˈʌndəɹ ɪt, ɐ fˈɪfθ əvə ʃˈiːt ɒv pˈeɪpə.

lines.text: So the bigger number doesn't block twice as much. It lets half as much in, when there's enough of it.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ðə bˈɪɡə nˈʌmbə dˈʌzənt blˈɒk twˈaɪs az mˈʌtʃ. ɪt lˈɛts hˈɑːf az mˈʌtʃ ˈɪn, wˌɛn ðeəz ɪnˈʌf ɒv ɪt.

lines.text: Next: why do fingers wrinkle in the bath, but not your arm?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wˌaɪ dˈuː fˈɪŋɡəz ɹˈɪŋkəl ɪnðə bˈaθ, bˌʌt nˌɒt jɔːɹ ˈɑːm?
